chunks.arabic_text: وَ رَوَى الْكَاهِلِيُّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ قَالَ:

translations.en: Al-Kahili narrated from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:

chunks.arabic_text: سَأَلَهُ رَجُلٌ وَ أَنَا عِنْدَهُ عَنْ قَطْعِ أَلَيَاتِ الْغَنَمِ قَالَ: «لَا بَأْسَ بِقَطْعِهَا إِذَا كُنْتَ إِنَّمَا تُصْلِحُ بِهِ مَالَكَ»

translations.en: A man asked him, while I was with him, about cutting the tails of sheep. He عليه السلام said: “There is no harm in cutting them if you are only improving your wealth by it.”

chunks.arabic_text: ثُمَّ قَالَ: «إِنَّ فِي كِتَابِ عَلِيٍّ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ أَنَّ مَا قُطِعَ مِنْهَا مَيْتٌ لَا يُنْتَفَعُ بِهِ».

translations.en: Then he عليه السلام said: “Indeed, in the Book of Ali عليه السلام, it is written that whatever is cut from it is dead and is not benefited from.”

en.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling that cutting the tails of sheep is permissible when done for the benefit of one’s property. At the same time, it establishes that the severed part itself is treated as dead flesh and is not to be used.
en.seo_question: Is it permissible to cut the tails of sheep in Shia fiqh, and what is the ruling on the severed part?

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm; it is permissible
key_terms.لَا يُنْتَفَعُ بِهِ: it is not to be used or benefited from
